newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA LEV DIPS ON LOWER T-BILL YIELDS, EYES PEG.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA LEV DIPS ON LOWER T-BILL YIELDS, EYES PEG.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev inched down to
984-988 per mark at close from opening's 983-987, preparing for
the 1,000-per-mark currency board peg from July 1 and pricing
in falling yields on government securities, dealers said.
* The lev closed at 1,700-1,702, a touch softer from the
morning's 1,695-1,700 as traders ajusted the lev/dollar rate to
the mark/dollar cross on international markets.
* Banks kept building up mark positions through mark/dollar
arbitrage abroad ahead of a launch of a currency board system
on July 1, when the mark is to become the anchor in the system.
* Banks' free lev liquidity was high but there were fewer
investment opportunities now that yields on government
securities have fallen sharply and the central bank was
expected to cut its main interest rate, now set at 35.76
percent annually.
* Dollar share in total daily interbank turnover has fallen
to 30-35 percent this month from 40-45 percent in May while
mark share has risen to some 15 percent from average five
percent.
* The average yield to maturity on benchmark four-week
discount T-bills fell to 0.69 percent at the daily auction on
Wednesday from 0.72 percent on Tuesday, 0.78 percent on Monday
and 0.90 percent on Friday, central bank figures showed.
* Falling yields signalled a pending cut in the central
bank main interest rate because the bank adjusts the rate to
the weighted average effective yield on the issues auctioned
daily from Friday through Thursday, traders said.
-- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 91188
